about.title: About Us
about.subtitle: Transforming scientific evidence into shields against disinformation.
about.historyDesc: Literacia Edu was born as an academic research project focused on solving one of the most pressing issues of the contemporary era: the vulnerability of young generations to fake news, disinformation, and online radicalization. Led by researcher Karoline Fernandes, the initiative evolved from academic theses and lab testing to become a Brazilian EdTech with social impact. Today, we unite national and international universities to bring media literacy to public and private schools, proving that science and playful education are the best paths to a healthy digital future.

mission.title: Our Mission
mission.desc: To empower children and adolescents to develop critical thinking and digital resilience, providing innovative educational tools based on scientific evidence.

vision.title: Our Vision
vision.desc: To be the leading global reference in educational solutions for youth media literacy and combating disinformation by 2030, integrating technology, psychology, and science.

items.title: Scientific Rigor
items.desc: All of our methodologies and games are built on top of active, peer-reviewed, and validated scientific research.

items.title: Educational Innovation
items.desc: We create learning experiences that truly resonate with young audiences through gamification.

items.title: Ethics & Transparency
items.desc: We promote truth, data privacy, and social responsibility in every project.

items.title: Social Inclusion
items.desc: We work actively to bring our tools to both private and public school systems.

about.scienceDesc1: Our solutions are based on the Luden method, created by Literacia Edu's research team and inspired by scientific principles from social psychology, serious games, and User-Centered Design (UCD) approaches. The word comes from the Latin ludere, meaning to play, to game, or to practice. The acronym unites the concepts that guide our values and principles: Literacy, Usability, Fun, and Engagement.
about.vacinaDesc: Media literacy at Literacia Edu is not passive. Based on Inoculation Theory, we teach manipulation techniques before young people experience them.
about.inoculacaoDesc: Like a vaccine that stimulates internal defenses, we present fake news techniques in a simplified way to develop critical thinking antibodies.

meiasVerdades.title: Meias#Verdades Mobile Game
meiasVerdades.subtitle: A cognitive vaccine against social media disinformation.
features: Social media simulator integrated within a secure environment.
Educational roleplay: students play from the malicious content creator's perspective to understand internal mechanics.
Modules based on real-world techniques: bot usage, hyper-emotional appeals, conspiracy theories, and artificial polarization.
Real-time media literacy progress metrics for educators.
meiasVerdades.audience: Recommended for middle and high schools (ages 11 to 17).

mockup.quote: "Share this lie to earn engagement points."
mockup.desc: The game challenges students to create posts with emotional appeal or scapegoating to teach the risks behind the easy click.

memoryGame.title: Meias#Verdades Memory Game (Offline)
memoryGame.subtitle: Game-based pedagogical interventions.
memoryGame.featuresTitle: Why use it in the classroom?
features: Perfect for schools with restrictions on smartphone use in the classroom.
Promotes face-to-face dialogue mediated by the teacher, developing soft skills such as cooperation and argumentation.
Card deck with exclusive illustrations and real problem situations adapted for collective debate.
Complete teacher guide for alignment with BNCC (competencies 4 and 5).
memoryGame.audience: Recommended for Elementary School I and II (8 to 14 years old).

livro.title: Meias#Verdades Book
livro.subtitle: Meet our methodology.
livro.desc: In the book Meias#Verdades: Learn to Unmask Disinformation Tactics and Combat Fake News!, researcher Karoline Fernandes discusses the most current theoretical concepts of disinformation and defends the application of the prebunking method in serious game design as an effective strategy to prevent people against online manipulation.
features: Based on the prebunking method (pre-demasking), originated from Psychological Inoculation Theory.
Doctoral thesis developed at PPGCI-UFPE with visiting research at KU Leuven University, Belgium.
Mental vaccine metaphor: weakened doses of disinformation to stimulate the production of "mental antibodies".
Available in physical format and e-book through Editora Appris (editoraappris.com.br and Amazon).
livro.audience: For educators, researchers, and communication professionals interested in scientific strategies against disinformation.

codigoPata.title: Código P.A.T.A.
codigoPata.subtitle: Animal Welfare Literacy
codigoPata.desc: The Código PATA project is a set of gamified educational interventions designed to teach children and adolescents about animal welfare. The project also included a series of microvideos with gamified missions so kids can learn how to take care of their pets!!

media.title: Startups gain space to do business with investors at Mangue.Bit
media.desc: The report covers the commemorative tenth edition of Mangue.Bit, an event held in Recife that brings together startups, investors and companies to stimulate business and strengthen the Northeast's innovation ecosystem. Among the initiatives presented is Literacia Edu, the startup founded by Karoline Fernandes that develops digital games and gamified tools to promote media and digital literacy for children and teenagers. Its main highlight is the game Meias Verdades, based on the prebunking strategy, which prepares users to recognize manipulation and disinformation tactics on social media in advance. The report also highlights the startup's expansion plans through an educational platform for public and private school networks, with gamified learning tracks for students and support tools for teachers.

media.title: To fight disinformation, journalists with a degree!
media.desc: Journalist Karoline Fernandes defends valuing higher education in Journalism as a path to strengthen rigorous reporting, professional ethics and access to quality information in the face of the spread of fake news.

media.title: Journalist and researcher launches book on how to protect yourself from fake news
media.desc: Karoline Fernandes' book Meias#Verdades presents scientific concepts about disinformation and proposes using prebunking and educational games to prepare people to recognize manipulation tactics before being deceived.

media.title: Journalist Karoline Fernandes launches book that teaches how to combat fake news
media.desc: The publication, the result of doctoral research at UFPE, explains how psychological inoculation can help the public recognize misleading content. The report also highlights the development of the educational game Meias#Verdades, aimed at children and teenagers.

media.title: Book by a Pernambuco researcher proposes creating “mental antibodies” against fake news
media.desc: The report covers the proposal of building resistance to disinformation through prebunking, a method that presents manipulation strategies in advance, with explanations and refutations. It also highlights the emotional and cognitive mechanisms behind accepting false information and the potential of educational games for developing critical thinking.

media.title: The Theory of Psychological Inoculation in the Meias Verdades Game
media.desc: The report covers the development of the digital game Meias Verdades by UFPE researchers, with a testing phase coordinated by Karoline Fernandes. The initiative is based on the theory of psychological inoculation, which works as a cognitive vaccine: by coming into contact with weakened versions of disinformation strategies and learning how they work, players build the ability to recognize manipulation attempts and resist misleading content in real life.

media.title: Prebunking, Media Literacy and Serious Games
media.desc: In an interview with TV Senado, Dr. Karoline Fernandes explains the limitations of after-the-fact fact checking (debunking) and highlights the importance of preventive strategies. Through prebunking and serious games, the proposal is to train participants to recognize five manipulation tactics: polarization, false identity, defamation, emotional appeal and conspiracy. The interview also stresses the need to bring media literacy into the school curriculum, promoting critical thinking and autonomy in the face of online information.

media.title: Cognitive Vaccine, Impartiality and Education Policies
media.desc: In an interview with Rádio Jornal, Dr. Karoline Fernandes highlights the cross-cutting nature of disinformation and its link with polarized environments and emotional appeals. As a response, she defends a preventive approach based on psychological inoculation and the development of cognitive skills.
